name: LodePNG
baseline: libpng 1.6.37 (with zlib 1.2.11, as shipped with Debian Bullseye)
workload: PNG decode throughput in MB/s on five test images (19k 8bpp, 40k 24bpp, 77k 8bpp, 552k 32bpp, 4002k 24bpp decoded size) in the Wuffs 'mimic' benchmarks, where lodepng 20220717 is swapped in for libpng behind the same decode harness.
claimed_speedup: Decode 1.13x (138 vs 122 MB/s, 19k_8bpp), 1.13x (166 vs 147 MB/s, 40k_24bpp), 1.09x (404 vs 370 MB/s, 77k_8bpp); but slower on the larger images: 0.89x (258 vs 289 MB/s, 552k_32bpp_verify_checksum) and 0.77x (165 vs 214 MB/s, 4002k_24bpp). Ratios are the page's vs_mimic column, libpng = 1.00x.
compiler_and_flags: clang 11.0.1 and gcc 10.2.1 (page does not say which one built the mimic rows); recipe in test/c/std/png.c is -O3 with -DWUFFS_MIMIC -lm -lpng -lz, and test/c/mimiclib/png.c has WUFFS_MIMICLIB_USE_LODEPNG_INSTEAD_OF_LIBPNG defined with lodepng.cpp #included. libpng 1.6.37 and zlib 1.2.11 are the Debian Bullseye system builds.
hardware: Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10210U CPU @ 1.60GHz, Debian Bullseye, measured September 2022
tradeoffs: Two-file C89/C++ library with no dependencies (lodepng.cpp/lodepng.h, rename to .c for C). Own inflate/deflate, so no zlib needed. Encoder and decoder are small and portable, but the project does not target peak speed; libpng/spng/stb/wuffs are the usual fast choices.
caveats: The project makes no speed claim; the numbers come from the Wuffs project's own mimic benchmark, not a lodepng-authored benchmark. Mixed result: lodepng wins by 9-13% only on the three smaller images and loses on the two larger ones (0.89x, 0.77x). Decode only; no encode numbers against libpng were reached (fpng's README and lodepng issue #179 show lodepng encoding at ~3-17 MP/s with no libpng row). The libpng baseline is the Debian system build linked to zlib 1.2.11, whose inflate is slow; a libpng built on zlib-ng or libdeflate would narrow the gap. lodepng version in the table is 20220717, older than the current repo. The page does not state which of clang/gcc built the mimic rows, and the mimic harness for lodepng does not support the ignore-checksum quirk. Tier A is by the rubric (public code, compilers and CPU stated); the verifier should weigh that the claim is only a partial win.
found_via: seed-record pass; started from https://github.com/lvandeve/lodepng (README has no speed claims), then WebSearch 'lodepng vs libpng decode encode speed benchmark MB/s comparison', which led to the Wuffs benchmarks page https://github.com/google/wuffs/blob/main/doc/benchmarks.md
